question: Which base case makes a recursive C++ reverse(string s) function correct for both an empty string and a one-character string?

answers.feedback: Correct. Both inputs are already their own reverse, and the empty-string case is safe.
This handles one character but misses the empty string; indexing or recursing from an empty input can then fail.
An empty string has no element at index 0.
This stops immediately for every nonempty input, so strings longer than one character are never reversed.
